projects.title: DeTerminator
projects.intro: I built and programmed Terry, an Arduino rover that measures carbon dioxide and humidity to investigate possible signs of termite activity. The project earned fourth place in individual Robotics and Intelligent Machines at the 2025 Division Science and Technology Fair.
projects.alt: Hands connecting wiring inside the DeTerminator rover beside its blue display

details.heading: The build
details.text: I programmed, integrated the hardware, and built the rover, named Terry. It collects environmental readings from sites where termite activity is suspected.

details.heading: The science fair
details.text: DeTerminator earned fourth place in the individual Robotics and Intelligent Machines category at the 2025 Division Science and Technology Fair in Bulihan, Silang, Cavite.

gallery.alt: Terry’s wiring layout, including the controller, sensors, breadboard, motor driver, display and power supplies.
gallery.caption: Terry’s circuit, drawn from my Cirkit Designer project. Open the diagram to inspect the wiring.

gallery.alt: Arduino Uno controller, MG811 carbon dioxide sensor, and the temperature and humidity sensor.
gallery.caption: The Uno reads the environmental sensors. Carbon dioxide and humidity were the two measurements I investigated.

projects.transcript: The original presentation introduces Terry, shows the rover and its assembly, and explains the research and results. The recording includes on-screen captions.
projects.overview: I built and programmed Terry, an Arduino rover for investigating termite activity.

projects.title: Shop Inventory Manager
projects.intro: Helping my mother at a canteen inspired me to build a sari-sari store inventory app with Java Swing and SQLite. The product form lets you change a price or stock count and see the updated item in the inventory table.
projects.alt: The Shop Inventory Manager product form and stock table in the original screen recording

details.heading: The idea
details.text: Helping my mother at a canteen inspired me to build a simple tool for tracking products, prices, and stock. I left supplier and item code fields out of the product form.

details.heading: The build
details.text: I built the desktop interface with Java Swing and used SQLite with DBeaver. A Project Tuklas Teknolohiya workshop on connecting Java to a database helped me apply the approach to this project.

gallery.alt: The complete Java desktop window with its product form, search controls and inventory table.
gallery.caption: The full Shop Inventory Manager interface.

gallery.alt: Product name, unit price and low-stock alert fields.
gallery.caption: Each product has a unit price and its own low-stock threshold.

gallery.alt: Inventory rows showing unit price, quantity, reorder level and stock status.
gallery.caption: The stock table shows which products are in stock and which have reached their reorder level.

projects.transcript: The recording shows the desktop product form and inventory table, including controls for adding and updating products and searching the stock list.
projects.overview: Helping my mother at a canteen gave me the idea for a desktop app to track products, prices, and stock in a sari-sari store.

settings.aboutHeadline: Computer Science student at Cavite State University.
bio: I’m interested in software development, robotics, databases, and cybersecurity. My goal is to become a software engineer and build a stronger foundation in data and technology.
I have basic knowledge of Java and Python, and hands-on experience with SQL and database management, Arduino programming, and robotics hardware.
